findings.title: Image proxy buffers the complete upstream body without a size bound
findings.tradeoffs: A limit may reject unusually large images that currently render. Stream buffering must preserve correct content type and failure/status behavior. Avoid restricting destination hosts or stripping authorization headers: callers intentionally use private and arbitrary self-hosted integration URLs.

details.change: Return the unchanged upstream response.body to the sole route consumer. Remove deliberate arrayBuffer materialization and size-based success logging. Keep encrypted registered URL/headers, trusted-certificate fetch seam, status/content type, SVG, and cache headers. Use a narrow documented stream type assertion at the Node/DOM type boundary.
details.caveats: Streaming changes when late read errors surface and removes a pre-header body-read failure boundary. The browser fallback and reverse proxy/cache behavior are not live-verified.; Sampled RSS/external/arrayBuffers growth is process-wide and GC-dependent. Lazy source allocation is inside the workload; separate tiny normal-image fixtures are excluded. No fixed-memory or exact transport backpressure bound is claimed.; Trusted-certificate fetch behavior is preserved at its existing dependency seam; actual TLS/private-service compatibility is not exercised.

findings.title: Assistant request size is checked after the body has been fully buffered
findings.tradeoffs: Adds stream-reading code and must handle cancellation/release correctly. Upstream reverse-proxy limits may reduce exposure but do not make the application-level check a body-read bound.

details.change: Count received encoded bytes before decoding each accepted chunk. Stop and cancel at the first chunk exceeding 12,000,000; preserve 413 even if cancel rejects; release reader lock in finally. Decode split UTF8 incrementally and retain only accepted decoded text. Keep declared oversized rejection before auth, authentication before stream consumption, and existing JSON/schema/attachment checks.
details.caveats: 12M is the intentional accepted byte ceiling, not an exact RSS bound. A largest delivered chunk, decoded strings, JSON parsing representations, ingress and transport queues can allocate more.; Large preallocated multibyte/exact-boundary semantic fixtures are excluded from the lazy memory workload.; Reverse proxy ingress limits and production frequency were not measured.

findings.title: Docker log lookup maps every API failure to a missing page

details.change: Catch typed TRPCError NOT_FOUND only for 404; rethrow every other failure to the existing error boundary. Preserve admin/feature guards and endpoint discovery behavior.
details.caveats: Semantic classification is verified without live Docker or browser boundary rendering. Endpoint-discovery catch remains intentionally unchanged.; No CPU performance claim for this error-semantics change.

details.change: Grow mobile settings target toward 44 physical pixels using canvas compensation; cap each dimension to fit the widget. Keep the desktop target, icon size, accessible name and Menu intact.

A constrained 32x32 physical widget retains 24x24 to avoid overflow.; Fixture uses real canvas and Mantine CSS with explicitly sized widgets, not a whole live dashboard. Arbitrary user CSS can override dimensions.
